title: Saudi Arabia Launches One-Year Multiple-Entry Umrah Visa With 90-Day Stay
excerpt: The new visa lets pilgrims visit Makkah and Madinah multiple times within 365 days, but each trip requires a fresh service package and Umrah permit booked through the Nusuk platform.
body:
• Saudi Arabia's new multiple-entry Umrah visa is valid for 365 days with a cumulative stay of up to 90 days across all visits
  • Pilgrims must purchase a service package through the Nusuk platform and obtain an Umrah permit before each entry
  • The visa automatically deactivates upon departure and cannot be used during the annual Hajj season
  • Indian pilgrims can apply through authorized agents or directly via the Nusuk platform if eligible for e-visa processing

Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Hajj and Umrah announced on July 20, 2026 a new multiple-entry Umrah visa valid for one full year from the date of issuance, according to the Saudi Press Agency. The visa allows pilgrims to enter the Kingdom multiple times with a combined stay of up to 90 days across all visits — a departure from the previous system that required a fresh visa application for each trip.

How the New Visa Works

Under the new framework, each entry requires two steps: the pilgrim must purchase an approved service package through a provider on the Nusuk platform, and they must obtain an Umrah permit through the Nusuk mobile application before arriving in Saudi Arabia. The duration of the service package cannot exceed the number of days remaining on the visa.

The visa automatically deactivates when the pilgrim leaves the Kingdom. It reactivates only after the traveller meets the regulatory requirements for a subsequent visit. The 90-day cumulative limit does not reset after each trip — it is a running total across the visa's full validity period.

One critical restriction: the multiple-entry visa will not be activated during the annual Hajj season, from the first day of Dhu Al-Qi'dah until the 13th day of Dhu Al-Hijjah. Pilgrims planning Hajj must obtain a separate Hajj visa.

Part of a Broader Overhaul

The initiative is part of Saudi Arabia's broader efforts under Vision 2030 and the Pilgrim Experience Program to simplify travel procedures and improve service efficiency for religious visitors. The Kingdom has been steadily digitizing its pilgrimage infrastructure through the Nusuk platform, which now handles visa applications, accommodation bookings, transport arrangements, and permit issuance in a single system.

"The new visa is designed to give pilgrims greater flexibility in planning their religious journeys while supporting the integration of digital and operational services across the entire pilgrimage experience."

— Saudi Ministry of Hajj and Umrah, via Saudi Press Agency

For the 2026 Umrah season, the rules have also tightened for single-entry visas. Pilgrims must now enter Saudi Arabia within 30 days of visa issuance, reduced from the previous 90-day window, though they can still stay for up to 90 days once inside. Travellers on a Saudi tourist e-visa may also perform Umrah outside the Hajj season without a separate Umrah visa.

What Indian Pilgrims Need to Know

India sends one of the largest contingents of Umrah pilgrims to Saudi Arabia each year. Under the new system, Indian passport holders can apply through authorized sub-agents approved by the Ministry of Hajj and Umrah, with visa processing typically completed within two to four working days. Indian communities in the Gulf, the UK, the US, and Canada are also eligible to apply through these channels.

The MenACWY meningococcal vaccine remains mandatory for every pilgrim aged one and above. Pilgrims must also link their visa application to confirmed accommodation and transport bookings within the Nusuk system.

What's Next

The move is expected to benefit millions of Muslims worldwide who make multiple Umrah visits per year, particularly families who travel together during school holidays or long weekends. Saudi Arabia has continued expanding religious tourism infrastructure despite broader regional disruptions, positioning itself as a year-round destination for Muslim pilgrims through streamlined digital services and flexible visa options.
nri_angle: India sends one of the largest Umrah pilgrim contingents each year, and the new multiple-entry visa eliminates the need for repeat applications, benefiting Indian Muslim families planning frequent visits.
